before: Training examples are used to adjust the model. Evaluation asks how well it works on examples it was not adjusted to match.
A validation set helps choose settings or compare candidate models during development.
A test set is held back for a later, separate check. Repeatedly choosing changes from test results makes it less independent.
If near-identical copies of the same example appear in training and testing, the test can look easier than genuinely new cases.
This accidental sharing is called data leakage. Separate related records carefully, not merely their file names.
after: Training data helps adjust a model. Evaluation means checking its results. To test how it handles new examples, use data kept out of training.
A validation set is a separate group of examples used to choose settings or compare models during development.
A test set is kept for a later check. If you keep choosing changes from its results, it becomes part of development and is no longer a fresh test.

Data leakage happens when information that should stay outside training or model selection gets used there. Keep copies and closely related records together when splitting data. Different filenames alone do not make a fair test.

before.question: You train on a photo and test on an almost identical copy. Why could a high test score mislead?
choices: The model is forbidden from recognizing any photo.
The test may reward remembering the training example instead of handling a genuinely new one.
Different file names guarantee independent evidence.
before.explanation: A renamed or duplicated example is not necessarily independent of training.

after.question: You train on a photo, then test on a nearly identical copy. Why might a high score mislead?
choices: Models are not allowed to recognize photos.
The test may reward remembering the photo instead of handling a new one.
Different filenames always make a fresh test.
after.explanation: A copy can be too similar to a training example to show how well the model handles new cases.
